segments.spokenText: فيه حقل جنب بركة، والمطر نزل بعد استخدام مبيد. ينفع نقول إنّ السمك اتضرّر؟ لسه. عندنا مصدر محتمل ومسار ممكن، لكن محتاجين دليل على وصول المادّة، وتركيزها، ومدّة التعرّض، والاستجابة البيولوجيّة. هنرتّب السؤال في أربع خانات: المصدر، وطريق الانتقال، والكائن المتعرّض، والأثر اللي هنقيسه. كلّ سهم في النموذج بيمثّل فرضيّة نختبرها. وجود رسم مقنع مش معناه إنّ كلّ خطواته حصلت فعلًا.

segments.spokenText: Assume a method with a detection limit of two thousandths of a milligram per litre and a quantitation limit of six thousandths. A below-detection report does not establish zero concentration; it reports a limitation under those measurement conditions. Four thousandths may be qualified as detected but below the required quantitation level. Do not remove the qualifier and treat the number as precise. Reporting codes vary by method, so consult the laboratory’s definitions.

segments.spokenText: A predator may consume many prey over its life. Efficient uptake combined with removal that is slow relative to intake can produce a higher tissue concentration. But not every chemical behaves this way. Chemical form, metabolism, diet and tissue basis all matter. There is no universal rule that residues increase by ten percent at every trophic level. Energy transfer is not a fixed equation for predicting a chemical concentration.

segments.spokenText: Use a hypothetical first-order model with an initial concentration of eight milligrams per kilogram. If the half-life is ten days under those model conditions, four remains after ten days and two after twenty. Each interval halves the remaining amount; it does not subtract four indefinitely. The equation is eight times one-half raised to the number of half-life intervals. In rate-constant form, half-life equals the natural logarithm of two divided by the rate constant. The model must fit the data and conditions.
